answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a mesa as the anchor of the cost.
